upheld.title: Search text lower-cased with the current culture
upheld.detail: name.ToLower() is evaluated on the server with CultureInfo.CurrentCulture, while c.Name.ToLower() is translated to Postgres lower(). Under a culture such as tr-TR, 'BIKING' lower-cases to 'bıkıng' and no longer matches 'explorer biking computer', so the two sides of the comparison can disagree.
upheld.requirement: Expected: steps 2-4 return the same items as step 1 regardless of case; culture-independent comparison of identifiers is the .NET idiom (CA1304/CA1311)

upheld.title: Comment restates what the code does instead of why
upheld.detail: The comment 'Names match from their start regardless of case.' repeats the code. The reason for this design (lower() + StartsWith keeps Npgsql's LIKE escaping, so % and _ in the search text stay literal, unlike ILIKE) is only in the story's Implementation Notes.
upheld.requirement: pr-check-style guideline 5: comments explain why, not what

upheld.title: Redundant assertions in TC-BUG-43-05 and TC-BUG-43-07
upheld.detail: TC-05 asserts DoesNotContain on a list already asserted empty (Assert.Empty(result.Data)); TC-07 asserts DoesNotContain for two names after Assert.Equal of the exact two-element name array. The extra lines cannot fail independently.

dismissed.title: Search text is lower-cased with the server's culture
dismissed.reason: Duplicate of OPUS-1-1 (same line, same cause, same fix), withdrawn by its critic. OPUS-1-1 is kept.
